item.observed: A budget of 80,000 riel is parsed as $80 rather than $20.
item.title: Dancers can still receive a kit over their budget — the new budget parser treats 'budget 80,000 riel' as 80 dollars and misses ordinary unstated-currency budgets

item.observed: An unaffordable drop line is reduced or removed while another cue can still be returned.
item.title: Dancers can lose the beat-drop firework when their budget is tight — fit_budget falls back to removing protected drop lines instead of reporting that the kit cannot fit

item.observed: Budget trimming can return a kit with just one retained cue.
item.title: Dancers can receive a 15-second kit with only one cue after price reductions — removed cart lines silently delete their cues without restoring the required four to six

item.observed: 'Select a track for your dance' is accepted as the six-word song field.
item.title: Dancers can see instructions or six-word text instead of a short song label — clean_song removes brackets but accepts instructions and exactly six words without checking the request

item.observed: The named song 'Any' becomes 'Your trending track'.
item.title: Dancers lose the title of named songs such as 'Any' — clean_song replaces any title containing certain ordinary words with the fallback

item.observed: A request without a parsed budget can return a cue whose item_id is absent from the cart.
item.title: Dancers can still receive cues for fireworks absent from their cart — reconciliation runs only when a budget was parsed

item.observed: One cue, seven cues or a cue at 40 seconds can be returned as a successful kit.
item.title: Dancers can still receive incomplete or unusable shot plans — the changed builder accepts any nonempty number of cues and clamps invalid timestamps

item.observed: A drop at second 8 with cues only at seconds 1, 3, 5 and 12 is accepted.
item.title: Dancers can still receive a shot plan with no effect on the beat drop — the changed builder never requires a cue at drop_second or checks its prominence

item.observed: A request naming 'Any' can be returned with song 'Your trending track'.
item.title: Dancers can still receive the wrong song — the changed cleaner never verifies the returned title against the request and replaces legitimate titles containing 'any'

item.observed: A smoke item's model-supplied effect can say 'gold fountain'.
item.title: Dancers can still be told an item produces the wrong effect — the changed cue builder takes its displayed effect description from the model

reason: Same song-title failure as earlier finding shard_review-R-BUG-031, refiled for changed backend.

item.observed: Four confetti cues can survive with qty 1 after trimming the confetti cart line.
item.title: Dancers can buy fewer one-shot fireworks than their cue sheet requires — budget trimming reduces quantities without reconciling repeated uses of the same item

item.observed: A scene chunk loaded after second 5 starts with earlier cues already expired or late.
item.title: Dancers can miss early fireworks and the opening orbit — the preview clock and beat start before the lazy-loaded 3D scene is ready

item.observed: A fountain at 0:14 keeps emitting indefinitely after the counter reaches 0:15.
item.title: Dancers see a changing final frame and continued particle generation after 0:15 — the capped clock never reaches late emitters' end times and animation loops continue

item.observed: Phone view's 62° vertical FOV excludes the fountain emitters at x = ±2.6.
item.title: Dancers can lose their fountains from the simulated TikTok shot — the 9:16 phone camera is too narrow to include the ground fountain positions

item.observed: Drop smoke uses 1.6× particle size and drop fountains use √3 velocity.
item.title: Dancers do not see a three-times-larger effect on the drop — the director supplies a 1.6× size and several effects apply only √3 or unrelated scaling

item.observed: Stage and Phone views use the same fixed 2D projection; dragging does nothing.
item.title: Dancers without WebGL cannot orbit or see the phone's perspective — the 2D fallback ignores view mode and has no drag handler

item.observed: A tall narrow viewport clamps frame width while retaining full height.
item.title: Dancers on tall narrow phones see a stretched phone preview — max-w-full clamps width without reducing the fixed-height 9:16 frame

item.observed: A cue at 7.5 seconds flashes and shakes before a drop at 8 seconds.
item.title: Dancers see the drop flash and camera shake before the beat — both preview renderers treat any cue within 0.6 seconds of drop_second as the drop

item.observed: A model cart quantity of 1,000,000,000 causes up to a billion synchronous reductions.
item.title: Dancers can lose service while an oversized model cart is budget-fitted — unbounded quantities drive a one-unit-at-a-time loop on the async server's event thread

item.observed: The preview has Replay but no Pause or Resume control.
item.title: Dancers cannot pause the shot preview to inspect a cue — the timeline advances continuously and exposes only Replay

item.observed: When AudioContext creation fails, the unmuted sound icon is shown but no beat can play.
item.title: Dancers receive a silent preview that looks unmuted — AudioContext creation failure is swallowed and the mute control remains active

item.observed: The changed shot kit card still provides no copy or share action.
item.title: Dancers still cannot copy or share their shot plan with their crew — the changed kit card adds Preview but no share or copy action

item.observed: A long unbroken generated word is still clipped by the card's overflow-hidden.
item.title: Phone users can still lose part of their song or filming instruction — unbounded generated words do not wrap inside the changed clipped kit card

item.observed: A 7.5-second drop is displayed as 0:08 in the changed card's badge.
item.title: Dancers can still fire fractional cues at the wrong moment — the changed kit card rounds drop seconds and the cue list rounds and groups nearby cues

item.observed: A second kit arriving during an open preview inherits fired-cue indexes from the first.
item.title: Dancers can see a mixed or incomplete preview when a new build finishes — the live kit prop changes without resetting the director's fired cues and timeline

item.observed: One fountain cue at the drop renders two sprays even when the cart has qty 1.
item.title: Dancers can see more fountains in the preview than their kit supplies — the 3D drop and 2D fallback draw sprays on both sides without consulting cart quantities

item.observed: A height-only resize leaves the 2D canvas backing height unchanged.
item.title: Dancers can see a stretched fallback scene after resizing — canvas height is updated only when its width changes

item.observed: A drop at 0:14 or later leaves the DROP label visible permanently at 0:15.
item.title: Dancers see DROP stuck over the final frame for late drops — the label timeout uses the timeline clock after it is capped at 15 seconds

item.observed: Opening the overlay leaves keyboard focus on the underlying Preview button.
item.title: Keyboard and screen-reader users can operate the hidden kit controls behind the preview — the fullscreen portal has no dialog semantics, initial focus or focus trap

item.observed: The mute button is always announced as 'Toggle sound' with no pressed state.
item.title: Screen-reader users cannot tell whether preview audio is muted — the icon-only toggle never exposes its state

item.observed: A height-only resize, or initial 300px width at DPR 1, retains the wrong backing height.
item.title: Dancers can see a stretched fallback scene — canvas height is updated only when its width changes

item.observed: A $1,000 budget is parsed as $1 and can produce a budget-too-small error.
item.title: Dancers with comma-formatted dollar budgets can receive a tiny kit or no kit — the dollar regex stops reading at the thousands separator
